domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: AI models capable of producing novel content (text, code, images, audio, synthetic data) by learning probabilistic statistical patterns from massive training datasets.

tier3.analogy: Like a master forgery artist who studies thousands of classical paintings to paint an entirely new, original artwork in the exact style of the masters.

tier4.compare: Generative AI vs. Discriminative AI: Generative AI creates brand-new realistic data instances, whereas Discriminative AI evaluates and classifies existing input data into categories.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: Threat actors use GenAI to generate targeted spear-phishing emails and polymorphic malware. Defense: Deploy prompt firewalls, AI output detection, watermarking, and human-in-the-loop validation.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: A deep learning model with billions of parameters trained on massive text corpora to understand, summarize, generate, and predict human language.

tier3.analogy: Like an omniscient research librarian who has read an entire university library and can answer questions by predicting the most helpful next word.

tier4.compare: LLM vs. SLM: LLMs offer broader zero-shot capabilities but require significant GPU resources and present larger attack surfaces; SLMs are lightweight and easier to secure.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: Indirect prompt injection via malicious web pages processed by an LLM agent. Defense: Enforce input sanitization, strict system prompt boundaries, and strict output privileges.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: A highly compact language model (typically under 10B parameters) optimized for specialized domain tasks, edge deployment, lower latency, and reduced computational overhead.

tier3.analogy: Like a dedicated medical specialist who knows everything about cardiology rather than a general practitioner who knows a little about everything.

tier4.compare: SLM vs. LLM: SLMs have a drastically reduced attack surface, can run locally on secure edge hardware, and cost less to audit, but lack broader general reasoning.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: On-device parameter tampering or quantization corruption. Defense: Validate model file checksums (SHA-256), enforce secure boot, and isolate execution environments.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: A deep learning architecture relying on self-attention mechanisms to process entire sequences in parallel, computing contextual relationships between token positions.

tier3.analogy: Like reading an entire document at once and instantly highlighting key context connections across pages, rather than reading word-by-word with a magnifying glass.

tier4.compare: Transformers vs. Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs): Transformers enable high-speed parallel GPU training over huge contexts; RNNs process sequentially and suffer from vanishing gradients.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: Context window flooding leading to denial of service (Model DoS) or attention degradation. Defense: Enforce token input quotas, rate limits, and context truncation controls.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: A dual-network framework where a Generator creates synthetic data and a Discriminator evaluates its authenticity, driving iterative performance through competition.

tier3.analogy: Like a counterfeit currency creator trying to pass fake bills past an expert detective; both continuously adapt until the counterfeits are indistinguishable from real money.

tier4.compare: GANs vs. Standard ML Classifiers: GANs use competitive training to generate synthetic outputs, while standard classifiers evaluate real data inputs against fixed categories.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: Adversaries use GANs to forge synthetic biometric markers (voice/face) to bypass MFA. Defense: Implement liveness detection, multi-modal verification, and spatial anti-spoofing.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: The process of taking a pre-trained base model and updating its weight parameters on a smaller domain-specific dataset to adapt its outputs for specialized tasks.

tier3.analogy: Like taking a general lawyer fresh out of law school and putting them through a intensive bootcamp specializing exclusively in intellectual property law.

tier4.compare: Fine-Tuning vs. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Fine-tuning alters model weight parameters permanently, while RAG retrieves dynamic external facts without updating model weights.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: Data poisoning during fine-tuning to insert backdoors or override safety guardrails. Defense: Enforce cryptographic provenance checks and clean dataset verification pipeline audits.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: A optimization technique that reduces the numerical precision of model weight parameters (e.g., converting 32-bit floating point FP32 to 8-bit integer INT8) to minimize memory footprint.

tier3.analogy: Like converting a high-resolution lossless audio file to an MP3 format—it drastically reduces file size with imperceptible loss in performance.

tier4.compare: Quantization vs. Pruning: Quantization reduces numerical precision of existing weights, while Pruning eliminates redundant or zero-value connections entirely.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: Quantization-induced accuracy degradation creating safety policy blind spots. Defense: Perform post-quantization model evaluation and guardrail validation tests prior to deployment.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: Removing unimportant weights, neurons, or attention heads from a trained neural network to decrease model size and speed up inference without impacting accuracy.

tier3.analogy: Like trimming dead or weak branches off an overgrown tree to concentrate energy on the strongest, most productive limbs.

tier4.compare: Pruning vs. Quantization: Pruning zeroes out and structurally removes non-essential weights; quantization compresses parameter storage precision across all weights.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: Over-pruning causing degradation in anomaly detection sensitivity for critical zero-day events. Defense: Establish baseline benchmarks and automated regression test suites.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: Top-level instructional rules configured by system developers that define the model persona, operational boundaries, behavioral policies, and strict output constraints.

tier3.analogy: Like security guard standing orders at a facility entrance establishing strict access rules before visitors are allowed inside.

tier4.compare: System Prompts vs. User Prompts: System prompts establish immutable operational safety rules, whereas User prompts represent variable inputs provided by end users.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: System prompt leakage via prompt injection tactics. Defense: Implement prompt firewalls, external guardrail filters, and separate system/user context handling.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: Prompt techniques providing zero examples (Zero-Shot) or a small set of exemplar inputs/outputs (Few-Shot) in the prompt to guide task performance without parameter updates.

tier3.analogy: Asking someone to solve a puzzle with zero explanation versus giving them two solved sample puzzles first to show them the expected pattern.

tier4.compare: Few-Shot Prompting vs. Fine-Tuning: Few-shot prompting guides behavior within the immediate context window, while fine-tuning updates parameter weights permanently.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: Injected malicious examples (Few-Shot poisoning) altering output handling logic. Defense: Enforce prompt template sanitization and restrict dynamic example insertion.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: A machine learning paradigm where an agent learns optimal decision policies through trial and error, earning rewards for desired actions and penalties for unwanted ones.

tier3.analogy: Training a dog using treats for following commands and a firm 'no' for bad behavior until the desired habit is internalized.

tier4.compare: Reinforcement Learning vs. Supervised Learning: RL learns dynamic behavior policies through environmental trial/reward, while Supervised Learning maps inputs directly to labeled static datasets.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: Reward hacking or RLHF poisoning where attackers influence feedback loops to promote toxic outputs. Defense: Implement multi-reviewer validation and automated safety evaluation pipelines.

domain: Domain 1.1: Basic AI Concepts Related to Cybersecurity

tier2.concept: A decentralized model training technique where edge devices train models locally on private data and transmit updated model weight gradients—rather than raw data—to a central server.

tier3.analogy: A team of detectives solving local cases in their own cities and sharing only their lesson summaries to update a shared playbook without revealing confidential witness files.

tier4.compare: Federated Learning vs. Centralized Learning: Federated Learning preserves data privacy by keeping training data localized on device, whereas Centralized Learning requires pooling data into a single repository.

tier5.attack_defense: Attack Vector: Model poisoning attacks via rogue participating edge nodes. Defense: Apply differential privacy, secure aggregation protocols, and robust anomaly detection on gradient updates.
